lead.label: 9f
lead.why: Abstract: 'compound 9f, which possesses 3,4-dimethoxyphenyl on C-3' carbon atom of isoxazoline ring, exhibited the highest COX-2 inhibitory activity, and also displayed the most potent cytotoxicity on MCF-7 cells (IC50 0.03 uM)'; also the compound used for apoptosis/Bax/Bcl-2/caspase-3 and docking/MD follow-up.

reactions.conditions: Aldol (Claisen-Schmidt) condensation: NaOH (2.5 equiv), MeOH, ambient temperature, 3 h; solid filtered, recrystallised from MeOH; 87%.
Oxone (5 g per 1 g), THF/water, ambient temperature, 2 h; extracted CHCl3, washed 10% NaHCO3; 89%. Oxidant supplies the two O atoms (sulfide to sulfone) but is a bulk oxidant, not listed as reactant.
NH2OH.HCl (4 g per 1 g aldehyde), 10% aq NaOH, 95% EtOH, 60 then 70 C reflux, 2 h; acidified with 6 M HCl, solid filtered; 57% for 8f.
reactions.source: Section 4.1.5 and 4.1.11 (general procedure for 8a-8g; 7a-7g stated commercially available)

reactions.conditions: In situ nitrile oxide (oxime + 5% NaOCl, aq/CHCl3, -10 to -5 C, dropwise over 20 min, then 1-2 h at rt) and 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition onto the exocyclic alkene of 6; recrystallised from MeOH; 42%.

notes: Regiochemistry (aryl nitrile oxide carbon bonded to the CH(Ar) carbon; O bonded to the spiro carbon) taken from the compound name 'spiro[indene-2,5'-isoxazol]' with 3'-aryl and 4'-(methylsulfonylphenyl). The paper notes 9f/9g were reported previously (ref 26) but this paper gives the full procedure. Two name variants printed for 9f (4'H-spiro[indene-2,5'-isoxazol]-1(3H)-one in text, 4'H-spiro[isoxazole-5',2-inden]-1-one in experimental). Racemic, no stereo stated. Oxime 8f yield 57% given as per list.
